notes: Access: robots.txt names ClaudeBot/Claude-Web/anthropic-ai (alongside GPTBot, PerplexityBot, etc.) in a shared bot-policy block that disallows /c/*, /products/*, /collections/*, /api/*, /customer*, /all-products, /sso/* -- this is NOT a blanket 'Disallow: /' and applies identically to the generic 'User-agent: *' block, so it does not trigger the policy_opt_out stop condition. The site's actual stable category taxonomy lives at flat top-level slugs (e.g. /christmas/, /christmas-decoration/) which are NOT covered by any disallow pattern, so Tier-1 direct HTTP fetch (curl) was used throughout; no escalation to Playwright/Claude-in-Chrome was needed and none was used. No login wall was encountered for any category page -- all loaded and returned exact product counts without authentication. Discovery: the main nav/mega-menu and even category-hub pages are entirely client-rendered (zero anchor links to sibling categories present in SSR HTML anywhere, including on /christmas/ itself), so the reliable discovery path was sitemap.xml -> sitemap-categories.xml (561 category slugs), manually reviewed in full for seasonal/holiday terms (Christmas, Xmas, Halloween, Diwali, Easter, Valentine, Thanksgiving, New Year, Eid, Holi, Rakhi, back-to-school, Advent, Fall/Spring/Summer/Winter, festive, holiday). Each candidate slug was fetched directly and qty read from the site's own '<N> of <N> products are displayed' summary text, cross-checked against the page's schema.org ProductCollection numberOfItems (matches whenever total <=30, the SSR-page-1 cap). Found: a Christmas taxonomy (13 non-empty categories) plus three unrelated genuine seasonal categories -- Back to School (168), Fall Cushions (257), Spring Cushions (216), Summer Cushions (256) -- all standalone flat top-level pages, not nested under any Christmas or 'Seasonal' hub. No Halloween, Diwali, Easter, Valentine's Day, Thanksgiving, New Year, Eid, Holi, or Winter category exists anywhere in the 561-slug category sitemap. Dropped as confirmed-empty (genuine ProductCollection PLPs, checked 2026-09-03, currently 0 products -- pre-season restock, consistent with Home Decor core's drop-zero-rows convention): Christmas styles (christmas-worlds/), Christmas Baubles & Tree Ornaments, Christmas Lights, Christmas Tree Decorations, Christmas Tree Toppers, Christmas Trees, Advent Wreaths. Excluded Wreaths & Garlands (wreaths-garlands/) -- flat 'Home > Wreaths & garlands' breadcrumb with no holiday name or Christmas nesting and currently 0 products; a generic product-type page never established as seasonal by the site's own taxonomy (rule 5/6). Excluded Small gifts (small-gifts/, 90 products) -- generic year-round gift category, not holiday-named. Excluded the numeric /collections/<id>/ and /c/<brand-slug>/ pages seen on the homepage/category sitemap -- these are individual time-limited flash-sale campaigns (Westwing's core business model), not a stable product category, and are exactly the paths robots.txt disallows for all bots. Deduplicated summer-cushions-2/ against summer-cushions/ -- identical h1 'Summer cushions' and identical qty (256) though different underlying Shopify Collection gid; kept /summer-cushions/ (canonical, no numeric suffix, matches the fall-cushions/spring-cushions naming pattern) and dropped the -2 duplicate per the shared overlap rule. Observed but deliberately did NOT act on a numeric coincidence: Christmas Textiles (22) = Christmas Bedding (4) + Christmas Blankets & Throws (9) + Christmas Table Linen (9); Christmas Table (52) = Christmas Tableware (43) + Christmas Table Linen (9). No breadcrumb, nav, or facet evidence anywhere establishes an actual parent/child relationship between these pages -- every page's breadcrumb is flat 'Home > [category]' with no intermediate node -- so all were kept as independent sibling leaf rows rather than collapsed into an invented hierarchy not evidenced by the site's own structure. Light naming normalization: prefixed 'Christmas' onto sub_category labels whose own <h1> omits it (h1 'Candles & candle holders' -> 'Christmas Candles & Candle Holders'; h1 'Decorative objects' -> 'Christmas Decorative Objects'; h1 'Christmas table' -> 'Christmas Table') since these pages are reachable only via christmas-*-prefixed URLs and this project's category field is not always visible alongside sub_category in downstream views; all other sub_category labels are verbatim site h1 text. Advent (advent-decoration/, h1 'Advent', 1 product) was classified under category Christmas as it is Christmas-season prep decor with no holiday of its own in the vocabulary. ADJUDICATION (2026-09-04): removed 'Fall Cushions' (257), 'Spring Cushions' (216) and 'Summer Cushions' (256) rows - these are a generic cushion product-type catalog sliced only by loose seasonal color/styling tags, not tied to any discrete occasion or shopping event (unlike Black Friday/Back-to-School), and each is far larger than the site's genuine 11-item Christmas Cushions row - ordinary merchandising rotation, not a genuine seasonal category per rule 5 (seasonal product type != seasonal category).
